about: Every recorded line in the games. The name on the left is the sound file; the words on the right are what the voice says. To change a line: edit the words, delete its sound file, and run tools/make-voice.py again. Only missing files are recorded, so nothing is paid for twice. A character whose voice id below is empty has not been given a voice yet, and their lines wait.

audio/g2/lesson/what-do-we-add-to-26-to-: What do we add to 26 to make 40? Count up from 26, and add up the jumps.
audio/g2/lesson/let-s-take-5-away-from-4: Let's take 5 away from 47. Split the numbers into tens and ones.
audio/g2/lesson/5-has-no-tens-so-the-ten: 5 has no tens, so the tens stay 40.
audio/g2/lesson/take-away-the-ones-7-tak: Take away the ones. 7 take away 5 is 2.
audio/g2/lesson/let-s-take-25-away-from-: Let's take 25 away from 47. Split the numbers into tens and ones.
audio/g2/lesson/take-away-the-tens-40-ta: Take away the tens. 40 take away 20 is 20.
audio/g2/lesson/here-s-a-trick-for-takin: Here's a trick for taking away. To work out 42 take away 17, count up from 17 to 42.
audio/g2/lesson/42-take-away-what-leaves: 42 take away what leaves 25? Count up from 25 to 42. The jumps tell us.
audio/g2/lesson/i-brought-my-coins-from-: I brought my coins from home in Canada! A nickel is 5 cents. A dime is 10 cents. A quarter is 25 cents.
audio/g2/lesson/start-with-the-biggest-c: Start with the biggest coin. 10 cents.
audio/g2/lesson/biggest-coins-first-then: Biggest coins first, then count on. That makes counting money easier!
audio/g2/lesson/start-with-the-biggest-c: Start with the biggest coin. 25 cents.
Start with the biggest coin. 2 dollars.
audio/g2/lesson/count-on-25-that-s-3-dol: Count on 25. That's 3 dollars and 25 cents.
audio/g2/lesson/count-on-10-that-s-3-dol: Count on 10. That's 3 dollars and 35 cents.
audio/g2/lesson/a-fig-costs-65-cents-and: A fig costs 65 cents and you pay with a loonie, 1 dollar. To find your change, count up from 65 cents to 1 dollar.
audio/g2/lesson/from-65-cents-to-70-cent: From 65 cents to 70 cents is 5 cents.
audio/g2/lesson/from-70-cents-to-1-dolla: From 70 cents to 1 dollar is 30 cents.
audio/g2/lesson/long-ago-people-in-egypt: Long ago, people in Egypt told the time with the sun. Let's think about how long things take!
audio/g2/lesson/we-measure-how-long-thin: We measure how long things take in seconds, minutes and hours.
audio/g2/lesson/a-second-is-very-short-i: A second is very short. It's about as quick as one clap.
audio/g2/lesson/a-minute-is-60-seconds-t: A minute is 60 seconds. That's about as long as counting slowly to 60.
audio/g2/lesson/an-hour-is-60-minutes-th: An hour is 60 minutes. That's much longer. Baking a loaf of bread takes about an hour.
audio/g2/lesson/a-boat-left-at-2-o-clock: A boat left at 2 o'clock and got to the next town at 5 o'clock. How long was the trip? Let's count the hours.
audio/g2/lesson/5-o-clock-is-3-hours-the: 5 o'clock is 3 hours. The trip took 3 hours!
audio/g2/lesson/opposites-are-words-that: Opposites are words that are as different as can be. Hot and cold are opposites.
audio/g2/lesson/try-them-in-sentences-th: Try them in sentences. The sand is hot. The snow is cold.
audio/g2/lesson/some-words-mean-the-same: Some words mean the same thing. Big and large mean the same.
audio/g2/lesson/swap-one-for-the-other-i: Swap one for the other in a sentence. A big pyramid. A large pyramid. It still means the same thing!
audio/g2/lesson/a-naming-word-called-a-n: A naming word, called a noun, names a person, a place or a thing. Here's a test: can you put 'the' in front of it? The pyramid. Yes! It's a noun.
audio/g2/lesson/an-action-word-called-a-: An action word, called a verb, is something you do. Test it: can you say 'I can' in front of it? I can dig. Yes! It's a verb.
audio/g2/lesson/a-describing-word-called: A describing word, called an adjective, tells us what something is like. A golden crown. Golden tells us what the crown is like.
audio/g2/lesson/a-scribe-had-to-spell-ev: A scribe had to spell every word the right way. Let's try!
audio/g2/lesson/some-sounds-are-spelled-: Some sounds are spelled with a team of letters. In rain, the A and the I work together to make the long A sound. In boat, O A makes the long O sound. In night, I G H makes the long I sound.
audio/g2/lesson/and-in-cake-the-e-at-the: And in cake, the E at the end is silent. It makes the A say its name.
audio/g2/lesson/some-words-have-a-tricky: Some words have a tricky part that doesn't sound the way it looks. We call them heart words, because we learn the tricky part by heart.
audio/g2/lesson/in-friend-the-tricky-par: In friend, the tricky part is I E. Look at it, say the letters, and remember it: F, R, I, E, N, D.
audio/g2/lesson/to-mean-more-than-one-mo: To mean more than one, most words just add S. One cat, two cats.
audio/g2/lesson/words-that-end-in-s-x-s-: Words that end in S, X, S H or C H add E S. One box, two boxes.
audio/g2/lesson/if-a-word-ends-in-a-cons: If a word ends in a consonant and Y, change the Y to I and add E S. One baby, two babies.
audio/g2/lesson/and-some-words-change-co: And some words change completely. One mouse, two mice!
audio/g2/lesson/to-talk-about-yesterday-: To talk about yesterday, most words add E D. Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped.
audio/g2/lesson/short-words-like-stop-do: Short words like stop double the last letter first. Stopped.
audio/g2/lesson/and-some-words-change-co: And some words change completely. Today I go. Yesterday I went. Say it in a sentence to hear which one sounds right.
audio/g2/lesson/let-s-read-about-egypt-l: Let's read about Egypt, long ago and today!
audio/g2/lesson/here-s-how-good-readers-: Here's how good readers find answers. First, read the question. Why were cats helpful?
audio/g2/lesson/then-look-in-the-scroll-: Then look in the scroll for the sentence that answers it. Cats kept mice away from the food.
audio/g2/lesson/so-cats-were-helpful-bec: So cats were helpful because they kept mice away. The answer was right there in the scroll!
audio/g2/lesson/the-pyramids-were-built-: The pyramids were built from rows and rows of stones. Let's count them the quick way!
audio/g2/lesson/here-are-3-rows-of-4-sto: Here are 3 rows of 4 stones. Counting them one at a time is slow. Let's count by fours instead!
audio/g2/lesson/that-s-the-same-as-4-plu: That's the same as 4 plus 4 plus 4.
